A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Ediacaran to early Cambrian high-grade metamorphism and crustal reworking in the southern granulite terrane is the result of the collision and accretion of the Dharwar Craton with an exotic crustal block, possibly the East African orogens.

the charnockites from the Ediacran−Cambrian high grade terranes in southern India formed through the melting of both juvenile and older crustal materials and that the juvenile component was mainly derived from a mantle source with a long crustal residence time.

the Southern Granulite terrain, south of the Palght-Cauvery sutter zone, comprises two crustal domains, one with a predominantly Neoarchean (2.5 Ga), and the other with a predominantly Ediacaran− Cambrian (0.6−0.5 Ga) metamorphic imprint, separated by an Ediacaran (0.75 Ga) crustal-scale shear system.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the southern Indian granulites represent a composite crustal assemblage, with the younger granulites being formed by a combination of recycling of older crustal components and the addition of juvenile crustal material, which was derived mainly from the mantle.

the southern granulite terrane is an amalgamation of several tectonic domains that formed during the Neoproterozoico-Cambrian, with the Madurai and Nagercoil block being the oldest, followed by the Trivandruam and Kollam blocks, and finally the Kanyakumari block, all of which amalgamated into a coherent crustal unit during the Ediacarano-Cambrian.
